techniques.name: Rolling Country-Rock Acoustic Strumming & Bass Strikes
techniques.description: Driving 4/4 acoustic strumming with accented root bass-note pick strikes on beats 1 and 3 translating Don Walker's rolling piano rhythm onto the guitar

sequence: Pluck the root bass note on beat 1 (open A string for A, open D string for D)
Follow with down-up sixteenth-note strums across the middle and treble strings
Transition cleanly into the F#m barre chord at the midpoint of each stanza
Accelerate into a brisk double-time feel during the final instrumental outro
tips: Use a single-finger mini-barre or three-finger cluster for the A major chord to allow quick changes to D
If the full F#m barre chord is tough at first, play F#m7 (2-X-2-2-2-0) with your thumb or index finger on the low E
Keep your strumming wrist loose so the tempo increase at the end feels natural
details.progression: A - D - A - E - F#m - D - A - E - A

techniques.name: Ian Moss Country-Blues Hybrid Double-Stops & 6ths
techniques.description: Sweet sliding 6th intervals across strings 1 and 3, combined with pedal-steel bends and vocal vibrato in A major pentatonic

notes: Sliding 6ths on strings 3 and 1: 6/7 -> 7/8 -> 9/10
Pedal steel bend: Hold fret 5 on B & high E while bending fret 7 G string up a full step
Target sweet C# major 3rd note at fret 6 on string 3
sequence: Fret the 5th-fret double stop with a flat index finger pad
Push the 7th fret G string with middle and ring fingers
Slide into 6th intervals on upbeats for singing country-rock bounce
tips: Use a Stratocaster in position 4 (neck + middle) for classic warm quack
Apply gentle compression to smooth out the dynamics between acoustic strums and electric fills
Keep bends strictly in pitch to maintain authentic pedal-steel sweetness

sections.name: Intro Don Walker Piano Hook & Acoustic Entry
sections.technique: Rolling Country-Rock Acoustic Strumming & Bass Strikes
sections.description: Don Walker's rolling barrelhouse piano is joined by the acoustic guitar establishing the jaunty A to D country-rock pulse.
notes: Pick the open A bass note cleanly on beat 1 before brushing the upper strings
Follow the bouncing sixteenth-note rhythm without rushing
Let the open E chord ring into Jimmy Barnes's opening lyric

sections.name: Verse 1 Post-Vietnam Narrative
sections.technique: Rolling Country-Rock Acoustic Strumming & Bass Strikes
sections.description: Iconic opening verse lines ('I left my heart to the sappers round Khe Sanh') over open A, D, and E chords.
notes: Maintain measured, intimate acoustic dynamics under Barnes's reflective storytelling
Target the root bass notes on beats 1 and 3
Let the E major chord hang with suspense at the end of line 2

sections.name: Verse Turnaround 'Last Plane Out of Sydney'
sections.description: The progression drops into F#m before climbing back through D and E to resolve on the legendary 'Last plane out of Sydney's almost gone'.
notes: Plant your index finger firmly across fret 2 for the F#m barre chord
Emphasize the quick A to E to A cadence on the punchline
Maintain the steady 100 BPM rolling pocket

sections.name: Mid-Song Dynamic Lift & Ian Moss Lead Fills
sections.description: Ian Moss begins peppering the narrative with sweet A major pentatonic double stops and singing fill licks between Barnes's vocal phrases.
notes: Blend the 5th-fret double stops on strings 1 & 2 with quick hammer-ons
Slide smoothly into the 7th-fret D note on string 3
Keep the touch light and vocal-like

sections.name: Ian Moss's Country-Rock Guitar Solo
sections.description: Ian Moss's melodic country-rock guitar solo. Weaves singing sliding 6ths on strings 1 & 3, pedal steel whole-step bends at the 7th fret of the G string while holding the 5th fret B string, and swift chromatic passing tones into the A tonic resolution.
sections.progression: A - D - A - E - F#m - D - A - E - A
notes: Bend the 7th fret G string while holding the 5th fret on strings 1 and 2
Slide up into the 6th intervals at frets 6/7 and 9/10 on strings 3 and 1
Execute rapid country-blues pull-offs down the A major pentatonic box
Resolve cleanly into the ringing open A chord as the verse returns

sections.name: Accelerating Outro Sprint & Double-Time Jam
sections.description: The band accelerates into a double-time country-rock sprint, with Don Walker's boogie piano and Ian Moss's ringing chords propelling the track to its celebratory climax.
sections.progression: A - D - E - A (repeating to final crash)
notes: Lock into the accelerating double-time rhythm without losing tempo discipline
Accentuate beats 2 and 4 to sync with Prestwich's snare roll
Conclude with a sharp, triumphant hit on the open A major chord

beginner.title: Open Chords & F#m Substitution
steps: Master the open A, D, and E major chord shapes
Practice the first half of the verse (A - D - A - E) at 80 BPM
Use F#m7 (2-X-2-2-2-0) if full barre F#m is still developing
Play through the full verse structure at 100 BPM

intermediate.title: Full Barre Chords & Bass-Strum Groove
steps: Execute the full 6-string F#m barre chord cleanly without buzz
Incorporate alternating root-fifth bass plucks before each down-up strum
Nail the quick A - E - A turnaround timing

advanced.title: Double-Time Outro & Lead Fills
steps: Weave Ian Moss style A major pentatonic fills between vocal lines
Drive the double-time outro strumming at high energy without fatiguing
Lead a full singalong performance with rock-solid dynamics

commonMistakes: Hesitating on the transition from E major to the F#m barre chord
Rushing the early verses before the song's natural dynamic build
Strumming the low E string accidentally during the D major chord

5 minutes: Bass-note plus strum pattern at 100 BPM
5 minutes: Full song playthrough including double-time outro
focusAreas: Dynamic storytelling from quiet verse to roaring outro
metronomeWork: Start at 80 BPM focusing on the E to F#m transition
Practice at album tempo of 100 BPM with accents on beats 2 and 4
Practice shifting smoothly into the double-time outro feel
